claims: search/packer/candidates/s182-1024.cert states s(182) <= 13970916436214678735385725854133/10^30 = 13.970916436214678735385725854133; issue #806 (opened 2026-10-25T04:16:24Z by evand) reports it rounded up at 12 places, 13.970916436215, 3.17e-3 below the register's 13.974090713122, and prints the SHA-256 of it and of s182-1024_regularized.cert.

Its JSON report states S_input 13.970916436217552 and S_exact 13.970916436214678735246016689770216761387128199672189143915867972, the side of a Newton-converged KKT point at 80 digits, with 885 active contacts, 68 corner-corner contacts, 176 load-bearing squares, 6 free squares (rattlers) and 43 frozen variables. The issue calls it a local minimum of the side, strict modulo 43 exact flat motions, with no corner-corner MILP descent, as numerical evidence at 80 digits, not interval proofs.

The issue calls it 'a new packing (a different local minimum from the register's 13.974090713), found by our explore loop from a start at n = 211: the register's s(211) packing (Daniil Ostashev; also in Francisco Couzo's repository)', and asks that the start be credited.

The issue says the source's two exact checkers, search/exact/verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), both print VALID, and that they share an author and the certificate format. s182-1024_regularized.cert is the same packing at the same side regularized for display, by the issue's word.

The issue quotes two Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard entries that state a side and no packing: 13.9727613470647 for Prathamesh Chavan (2026-10-23 08:32 UTC) and 13.9709164362306 for Subramanya N (2026-10-24 18:41 UTC), 'the same local minimum, very likely', listed about four hours before the source's search found it, independently as far as the author knows. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
